_meta.name: gas-install-editor-addon
_meta.description: Install an Apps Script EDITOR ADD-ON into the signed-in Google account via Deploy > Test deployments, so its onOpen()/createAddonMenu() menu appears in a Google Doc under Extensions > <add-on name>. Parameterised by script_id, so it works for ANY editor add-on project, not just Playmaker. Asserts the ACTIVE Google account before touching anything. Idempotent: every state-changing click is gated on the control's own ARIA state, so a re-run neither un-selects the deployment type nor double-creates a test.
_meta.author: Yeshie session 2026-08-02
prerequisite: Relay up + extension connected: curl -s http://localhost:3333/status -> {"ok":true,"extensionConnected":true}.
Chrome signed into the target Google account (this recipe never logs in and never types a credential).

HARD PREREQUISITE - FOREGROUND: the script.google.com tab MUST be the ACTIVE tab in a FOREGROUNDED Chrome window before the run. Do both: `open -a "Google Chrome"` then `POST http://localhost:3333/tabs/activate {"tabId": <id from GET /tabs/list>}`. See anomaly BACKGROUND-TAB-BREAKS-TRUSTED-CLICKS - the Drive picker step provably cannot work otherwise.

The document named by params.doc_title must already exist AND be old enough to appear in the Drive Picker's Recent list (see anomaly PICKER-INDEX-LAG). Create one with `navigate https://docs.google.com/document/create?title=<urlencoded title>` and give it several minutes.
_meta.whatThisFlowActuallyIs: The task brief described this as 'Deploy > Test deployments > Install'. That is the GOOGLE WORKSPACE ADD-ON flow. For an EDITOR ADD-ON (a script whose onOpen() calls DocumentApp.getUi().createAddonMenu()) there is NO 'Install' button and NO 'Uninstall' button anywhere in the Test deployments dialog - observed live, full dialog textContent captured 2026-08-02. The editor-add-on equivalent is: select deployment type 'Editor Add-on' -> 'Create new test' -> choose a Version, a Config, and a REQUIRED Test document -> 'Save test'. The saved test is what makes the add-on menu appear. Anyone looking for an Install/Uninstall toggle here will not find one.
_meta.verificationByConsequence: Open the chosen test document, click the Docs menubar item #docs-extensions-menu, then read '.goog-menu.goog-menu-vertical:not([style*="display: none"])'. BEFORE (baseline captured live 2026-08-02 on a fresh doc): 'Add-ons►Apps Script(E)AI Video Generator - Text to Video by Veo 3►'. AFTER: that string must additionally contain the add-on's name (for the Playmaker project, 'Playmaker'), and its submenu must contain 'Open Playmaker assistant'. A closed dialog is NOT proof. The test row appearing in the Test deployments table is a necessary-but-not-sufficient intermediate signal.

humanGate.what: Google OAuth consent for the add-on's scopes.
humanGate.whenItFires: NOT during this recipe as far as any run on 2026-08-02 observed - no consent screen appeared at any point through 'Save test'. It is expected the FIRST time the add-on actually RUNS in a document (Extensions > <add-on> > <menu item>), because that is when Apps Script needs the scopes.
humanGate.whatItAsks: For the Playmaker project the manifest at ~/Projects/playmaker/gdocs-addon/appsscript.json declares NO oauthScopes array, so Apps Script infers scopes statically from the code. The brief's four scopes (documents.currentonly, script.container.ui, script.external_request, drive.file) are NOT declared in the pushed manifest - flagged, not fixed (playmaker/ is read-only to this recipe).
humanGate.rule: YESHIE MUST NOT CLICK IT. Approving an OAuth scope grant is the user's decision. Navigate up to the consent screen, leave it on screen, and report which button the user must press ('Continue' / 'Allow' on accounts.google.com). Everything before and after that click is automatable.

anomalies: BACKGROUND-TAB-BREAKS-TRUSTED-CLICKS (the big one, generalises far beyond this site). When the target tab is not the ACTIVE tab of a FOREGROUNDED Chrome window, getBoundingClientRect() inside that tab returns a STALE layout, so trustedCoordClick computes stale coordinates and the click lands on nothing. Measured live and reproducibly: the SAME selector for the Test-document picker button resolved to x=1111,y=595 with the tab foregrounded (picker opened, 3/3) and to x=1046,y=564..592 with it backgrounded (picker never opened, 5/5). The step still reports status 'ok' with {ok:true,x,y} - a trusted click CANNOT tell you it missed. Only the response signature catches it. Fix: `open -a "Google Chrome"` + POST /tabs/activate before the run.

GOOGLE PICKER REQUIRES A REAL USER GESTURE. Non-trusted element.click() on the Test-document picker button returns ok and does nothing - no iframe, no overlay (verified: chain reached the click, then wait_for iframe[src*='picker'] timed out at 30s). Only trusted:true (CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent) opens it, and only when foregrounded.

THE DEPLOY DROPDOWN IS A TRAP - SKIP IT. click_text 'Deploy' + click 'Test deployments' failed ~50% of runs ('Element not found for trusted click: Test deployments' even with a 20s retry window), because the Deploy button toggles and a mistimed click closes the menu. But [role='menuitem'][aria-label='Test deployments'] is present in the DOM from first paint with a ZERO rect, and a NON-trusted element.click() on it opens the Test deployments dialog directly, with the dropdown never opening. 4/4 successes. Prefer the hidden menuitem over the visible menu.

THE OLD 'CONFIRMED BLOCKER' IS RETIRED. deploy-apps-script.payload.json records the deployment-type [role='menuitemcheckbox'] as a CONFIRMED BLOCKER needing a new jsaction_trigger action. That is false on the 2026-08-02 runtime. [role='menuitemcheckbox'][aria-label='Editor Add-on'] flips aria-checked to 'true' with BOTH trusted:true (verified once) AND plain non-trusted element.click() (verified 4x). No new action type is needed. The likely original cause was target mis-resolution / a mistimed click, not jsaction. (The bonus re-test of the literal 'Web app' checkbox in the New deployment dialog was descoped after a watchdog stall; the Editor Add-on checkbox is the same control family in the same menu.)

DEPLOYMENT TYPE DOES NOT PERSIST ACROSS DIALOG OPENS. Reopening Test deployments always returns to 'Please select a deployment type' with aria-checked='false' (verified). So the type click is effectively fresh each run - but it is still gated on aria-checked here, because a blind click would UNCHECK it in any future build where it does persist.

aria-expanded ON THE GEAR IS THE ONLY RELIABLE OPEN/CLOSED SIGNAL for the deployment-type list. [aria-label='Enable deployment types'][aria-expanded='true'|'false']. The list has no display:none / aria-hidden marker on its [role='menu'] (probed: [role='menu'][style*='display: none']:has(...) and [role='menu'][aria-hidden='true']:has(...) both never match). Clicking the gear when the list is already open CLOSES it - hence the read-gate on aria-expanded='false'.

wait_for state.visible IS NOT A VISIBILITY CHECK. background.ts: `if (step.state.visible !== undefined) return { matched: step.state.visible ? !!el : !el }` - it is pure existence. Cost an hour here: [role='menuitemcheckbox'] 'passed' a visible:true wait while having a zero rect. To test real visibility, attempt a trusted click (trustedCoordClick filters zero-rect elements) or read the ARIA state.

onError:'continue' IS NOT A THING. The executor honours `optional: true` ONLY (background.ts ~line 3265). A step with onError:'continue' still hard-fails the whole chain. Several exploratory runs died on this.

wait_for WITH onTimeout:'continue' ALWAYS REPORTS status 'ok'. The real answer is the `timedOut: true` field on the step result. Any probe that ignores timedOut is reading noise - this silently invalidated a whole round of selector probing.

js STEPS IGNORE step.frame. `js` with frame:'picker' resolves the frameId but PRE_RUN_DOMQUERY still ran in the TOP document (pageScan() returned url=script.google.com while the picker iframe was open). click / click_text / type / read DO honour frame. Use `read` with frame for picker introspection, never `js`.

PICKER-INDEX-LAG. The Drive Picker's Recent list and its search index lag file creation by MINUTES. A Doc created at T did not appear in Recent, in My Drive, or in picker search at T+42min for one doc; a second doc appeared under 'Today.' in Recent at roughly T+10min. Meanwhile drive.google.com/drive/my-drive showed both immediately. The picker's My Drive list is also alphabetical AND virtualised (rendered A..S only, ~2.7KB of text), so a Y-named file is not reachable without scrolling. Recent (the default tab) is the workable surface - once the file has propagated.

PICKER SEARCH IS FUZZY AND UNTRUSTWORTHY. Searching 'AAAA' returned "Copy of Zorina's Book". Searching the exact full title returned 'No matching results' while the file was already listed under Recent. Do not gate on search.

SAVE TEST SILENTLY NO-OPS WITHOUT A TEST DOCUMENT. Clicking 'Save test' with the Test document field empty returns ok, shows no error text (dumpText('required') and dumpText('error') both empty), and creates nothing - the dialog is byte-identical before and after. The document is mandatory; the UI just will not say so.

THE TEST DOCUMENT INPUT IS DISABLED. input[aria-label='Test document'] exists but matches [role='dialog'] input[disabled] and not input[readonly]; typing a doc URL or ID into it changes nothing. The Drive picker is the only way to populate it.
COMMENT ENTRIES EXECUTE. {"_": "PHASE ..."} entries run as real steps and come back status 'unsupported' with a null stepId. Harmless for goalReached/success; just expect them in stepResults.

WATCHDOG STALL 2026-08-02: the exploratory session stalled long enough for a 600s stream watchdog to fire. Cause was the driver harness, not the payload: a shell poll loop (`until status != running`) wrapped around a ~4-minute chain, plus a `sleep`-based poller that the tool layer blocks, plus one Chrome/extension churn event that flipped /status extensionConnected to false mid-poll ('Frame with ID 0 was removed' on the next navigate). Drive long chains with POST /run/async and poll from a SEPARATE short-lived command; never block a single command for the whole chain.

SOLVED 2026-08-03 (was the recipe blocker): the Drive picker commits on DOUBLE-CLICK of the file row. A single click only highlights it — the Test document field stays "No document selected" and Save test stays disabled. There is NO "Select"/"Open"/confirm button in this picker variant, which is why click_text "Select" always returned Element not found. Two prior attempts were hunting for a control that does not exist. Verified end to end via CDP: double-click -> field reads the filename, Save test enables, picker closes, and Save created a real Saved Tests row.

SCOPE, confirmed 2026-08-03 against Google docs AND by direct experiment: an Editor Add-on test deployment applies ONLY to the single "Test document" chosen when creating the test. It does NOT install the add-on across the user's documents. With an "Installed for current user" test saved against document A, Extensions in document B has no entry. The Config values (Installed for current user / Enabled in current document / Installed and Enabled) select the AUTHORIZATION STATE to exercise, not the document scope. Reaching every document requires publishing (Marketplace listing, unlisted is fine). Do not use this recipe expecting fleet-wide install.
The Config combobox already DEFAULTS to "Installed for current user", so no interaction with it is needed for the common case.

The Test deployments dialog exposes its whole state as text, including the Saved Tests table (columns Version | Enabled | Document). Verify a save by reading a row out of that table; "Enabled=False" is correct and expected for an Installed-for-current-user test.

Plain element.click() opens the Deploy menu but does NOT activate the menu items inside it — the menu closes with no dialog. Real CDP input dispatch (Input.dispatchMouseEvent, i.e. an a11y-tree click) does activate them. This is the opposite of the deploy-type checkbox, where element.click() works fine, so neither approach is universally right on this page.
notForThisRecipe: This recipe never grants an OAuth scope and never enters a credential. If an 'Authorization required' / 'Continue' / 'Allow' screen appears at any point, STOP and hand it to the human.
